legal_question_or_issue: How far does Article 9(1)-(9) (Chapter III, Section 2) – Risk management system translate the risk assessment principle into an enforceable obligation?
mandatory_or_discretionary_language: Coded mandatory; see exact_text and verification_notes for the operative wording.
scope_and_addressees: High-risk AI systems (classified under Art. 6 and Annexes I/III). Risks covered are limited to those that can be reasonably mitigated or eliminated through development, design or adequate technical information (Art. 9(3)). Art. 9(9) requires consideration of impacts on persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups.
commencement_and_temporal_application: Legally adopted but not yet applicable
responsible_actor_analysis: AI provider (of high-risk AI systems)
enforcement_route_and_remedies: Art. 16(a) (cons. p. 28; OJ p. 62) obliges providers to ensure compliance with Chapter III Section 2 (Arts 8-15). Non-compliance with Art. 16 provider obligations is subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Art. 99(4)(a), cons. p. 116; OJ p. 115; unchanged by 2026/1744). For SMEs, including start-ups, the lower of the two applies (Art. 99(6), OJ p. 116). The Act sets maxima; Member States lay down the penalty rules and enforce them (Art. 99(1), OJ p. 115). Ex ante conformity assessment (Art. 43, cons. p. 53; OJ p. 78); market surveillance (Art. 74, cons. p. 91; OJ p. 102) and procedure for AI systems presenting a risk (Art. 79, cons. p. 104; OJ p. 106).
researcher_legal_analysis: Providers must run a documented, continuous and iterative risk management process across the whole lifecycle of a high-risk AI system. It covers identifying and analysing known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety or fundamental rights, estimating risks under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse, evaluating risks from post-market monitoring data, and adopting targeted mitigation measures so that residual risk is judged acceptable. Systems must be tested, including before being placed on the market, against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds (Art. 9(6)-(8)). Providers must consider likely adverse impacts on persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups (Art. 9(9)).
provisional_conclusion: In the EU, this risk assessment provision is mandatory (procedural) within an instrument coded as binding legislation; its enforcement linkage is cross-referenced (statutory enforcement), and implementation is coded as not assessed.

legal_question_or_issue: How far does Rule 3(3) (Due diligence in relation to synthetically generated information), clauses (a) and (b); read with rule 4(1A) for significant social media intermediaries translate the transparency principle into an enforceable obligation?
mandatory_or_discretionary_language: Coded mandatory; see exact_text and verification_notes for the operative wording.
scope_and_addressees: Synthetically generated information: audio, visual or audio-visual information artificially or algorithmically created, generated, modified or altered so that it appears real, authentic or true (rule 2(1)(wa)). Applies to intermediaries under the IT Act, 2000; additional duties for significant social media intermediaries.
commencement_and_temporal_application: In force (from 20 February 2026)
responsible_actor_analysis: Intermediaries offering a computer resource that enables the creation, modification or dissemination of synthetically generated information; significant social media intermediaries (rule 4(1A))
enforcement_route_and_remedies: Due-diligence obligation under the IT Rules: under rule 7, if an intermediary fails to observe the Rules, 'the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 79 of the Act shall not be applicable to such intermediary' (loss of safe-harbour protection), exposing it to liability under the IT Act and other law. Takedown and blocking powers under the IT Act also apply.
researcher_legal_analysis: Intermediaries whose services enable the creation or dissemination of synthetically generated information (SGI) must use reasonable technical measures to prevent unlawful SGI, label lawful SGI prominently, embed permanent metadata or other provenance mechanisms, and prevent labels and metadata from being removed. Significant social media intermediaries must also require users to declare whether content is SGI, verify declarations with technical measures and display a label where content is confirmed as SGI (rule 4(1A)).
provisional_conclusion: In India, this transparency provision is mandatory (substantive | reporting) within an instrument coded as binding legislation; its enforcement linkage is cross-referenced (statutory enforcement), and implementation is coded as partially implemented.
